squawks.headline: BoE's Mann says a risk-management approach to policy is appropriate given inflation risks
squawks.detail: MPC member Catherine Mann said a risk-management strategy is suitable in light of the risks to inflation. No market reaction was reported in the inputs.

squawks.headline: French budget watchdog HCFP calls 2027 growth forecast optimistic but finds 2026 deficit target plausible
squawks.detail: France's High Council of Public Finances (HCFP) says the 2026 deficit target is plausible but carries risks. It describes the 2027 budget targets as a significant adjustment and says the deficit goal is a minimum given the country's alarming public finances.

squawks.headline: ECB's Nagel says the bank's tools are aimed at price stability, not at particular bond yield levels
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Nagel made the remarks when asked about the rise in bond yields. They come during a sell-off in euro area government bonds.

squawks.headline: Trump tells Time that high rates hurt the economy more than inflation and some inflation helps pay down debt
squawks.detail: In an interview with Time, US President Trump also said the US will soon be refilling its strategic oil reserves. The interview comes with the US 10-year Treasury yield at its highest level since 2002.

squawks.headline: French finance minister presents 2027 budget with €43bn of new measures, €54bn in total, and keeps 3% deficit goal for 2029
squawks.detail: French Finance Minister Lescure said the 2027 budget has €43bn of new measures, or €54bn including measures already in place, and that cutting the deficit to 3% of GDP by 2029 is still possible. Budget Minister Amiel said action on the budget cannot wait until next year's election.

squawks.headline: UK announces new sanctions on vessels suspected of carrying Russian LNG
squawks.detail: The UK government's latest Russia sanctions package targets shadow fleet ships believed to be transporting Russian liquefied natural gas. The same package also covers Russian military and intelligence officers accused of abusing civilians in Ukraine.

squawks.headline: French 10-year OAT auction yields 4.93%, up from 4.23%, with bid-to-cover dropping to 2.0 from 2.28
squawks.detail: At the same French government bond sale, the 20-year OAT priced at 5.4%, up from 4.74% at the previous auction, and its bid-to-cover fell to 2.43 from 3.07.

squawks.headline: UK September final manufacturing PMI comes in at 51.9, below the 52.0 forecast and down from 52.0
squawks.detail: The final UK manufacturing PMI for September was 51.9. The forecast was 52.0 and the previous reading was 52.0. The 2-year gilt yield stood at 3.92% and the 10-year at 4.578% in the latest snapshot.

squawks.headline: Italian 10-year yield rises 10bp to 4.7232%, its highest since November 2023
squawks.detail: Italy's 10-year government bond yield reached 4.7232%, up 10bp on the day and its highest level since November 2023, according to a market wire.

squawks.headline: UK 30-year gilt yield rises above 6%
squawks.detail: A market commentator reported shortly after 08:15 UK time that the 30-year gilt yield had moved above 6%. The FTSE 100 was reported down 2% at about the same time.

squawks.headline: French 5-year CDS climb to 71.6bp, the highest since July 2013, as French bonds sell off
squawks.detail: France's 5-year credit default swaps reached 71.6bp, their highest level since July 2013. The move came as French government bonds sold off.

squawks.headline: French PM targets €43bn in new budget savings, BFM TV reports
squawks.detail: French broadcaster BFM TV reports that the prime minister is seeking €43bn of fresh savings in the budget. The report comes as France plans record bond issuance next year, with debt at about 119% of GDP.

squawks.headline: Eurozone September final manufacturing PMI is revised up to 52.9 from the 52.7 flash reading
squawks.detail: The final eurozone manufacturing PMI for September came in at 52.9. Both the forecast and the previous reading were 52.7.

squawks.headline: US reportedly presses France and Germany to release emergency diesel stocks, raising the prospect of a US diesel export ban
squawks.detail: Three sources say the US has told France and Germany to release emergency diesel reserves or face a possible US ban on diesel exports. One source says the US wants the EU to release 120 million barrels of diesel over the next six months.

squawks.headline: US Treasuries end their worst quarter since 1994 as yields hit two-decade highs for a seventh straight session
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that US yields reached two-decade highs for a seventh consecutive session on Thursday. A fall in oil prices later steadied bond markets.

squawks.headline: Chinese refiners suspend October fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau until further notice, sources say
squawks.detail: Reuters, citing four people briefed on the matter, reports that Chinese refiners have stopped exporting oil products to destinations other than Hong Kong and Macau until Beijing says otherwise. One refiner has cancelled cargoes.

squawks.headline: Japan PM Takaichi pledges to control total annual JGB issuance across initial and supplementary budgets
squawks.detail: Japan's Prime Minister said the government will manage total annual government bond issuance, counting both the initial and the supplementary budgets. Earlier in the session, 10-year and 30-year JGB yields had risen to 3.110% and 4.200%.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield rises further to 5.33%, its highest level since 2002
squawks.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.33%, above the 5.304% reported earlier, according to a market wire post. The 10-year gilt yield stood at 4.578% in the latest snapshot.

squawks.headline: Swiss September CPI rises to 1.0% y/y from 0.8%, matching forecast
squawks.detail: Swiss annual consumer price inflation was 1.0% in September, in line with the 1.0% forecast and up from 0.8% the previous month.

squawks.headline: UK Nationwide house prices fall 0.2% m/m in September; annual growth slows to 0.8% from 1.6%
squawks.detail: Nationwide reports September house prices fell 0.2% on the month, against a forecast of 0.0% and a 0.2% rise previously. The annual rate eased to 0.8% from 1.6%.

squawks.headline: JGB yields rise across the curve: 10-year up 5bp to 3.110%, 30-year up 6bp to 4.200%
squawks.detail: In Asian trading, Japan's 10-year government bond yield rose 5.0bp to 3.110% and the 20-year rose 4.5bp to 3.945%. The 30-year yield gained 6.0bp to 4.200%, and dollar/yen rose 0.5% to 158.19.

squawks.headline: RBA Financial Stability Review says high asset prices and leverage leave global markets open to a sharp correction
squawks.detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia says the main threats to domestic financial stability come from overseas, and that more leveraged investors in bonds and equities add to volatility. It says private credit is not currently a risk to overall stability and that about 2% of owner-occupier borrowers face cash-flow shortfalls.

squawks.headline: US Secretary of State Rubio orders Iran's UN delegation out of the US as negotiations reach deadlock, Axios reports
squawks.detail: Axios reports that Rubio called for the Iranian delegation to leave the US after the UN General Assembly ended, with US-Iran negotiations at a deadlock, according to a US official.

squawks.headline: BoJ September summary of opinions shows several members favour further rate rises, with one saying hikes should speed up if inflation…
squawks.detail: In the Bank of Japan's summary of its September meeting, one member said the terminal rate could end up above estimates and market expectations, and another said the Bank should not be overly cautious given upside risks to inflation. A Cabinet Office representative said the government expects the BoJ to weigh the cumulative impact of past rate increases.

squawks.headline: BoJ Tankan: large manufacturers index rises to 24, short of 25 forecast; large non-manufacturers falls to 35
squawks.detail: The Bank of Japan's September Tankan put the large manufacturers index at 24, up from 22 but below the 25 forecast. The large non-manufacturers index fell to 35 from 37 against a 36 forecast, and firms expect consumer prices to rise 2.6% over a year, down from 2.7% previously.

squawks.headline: France plans record bond issuance next year with debt at about 119% of GDP
squawks.detail: France said it will sell a record amount of government bonds next year, according to Semafor, which reported that the French spread over German bonds widened after the announcement.

squawks.headline: Fed's Kashkari says inflation must return to 2% after a long overshoot and warns supply shocks could lift expectations
squawks.detail: Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari said the Fed must bring inflation back to 2% given the extended period above target, and that rolling supply shocks risk raising inflation expectations. He also described the rise in bond yields as a global trend.

squawks.headline: UK and EU agree to hold November summit, pushing talks on industrial subsidies into next year
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the UK and Brussels will go ahead with a key summit in November. The two sides have agreed to defer negotiations on industrial subsidies until next year.

squawks.headline: Trump says Fed Chair Powell should be forced to resign and asks the Attorney General to review a Fed report
squawks.detail: US President Trump said Federal Reserve Chair Powell should be forced out and asked Attorney General Blanche to review a Fed report. The inputs report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.304%, its highest level since May 2002
squawks.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.304%, rising from the 5.29% level reported earlier in the session and reaching its highest since May 2002. The UK 10-year gilt yield stands at 4.578% in the latest snapshot.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield climbs to 5.29%, a fresh high since 2007
squawks.detail: A market commentator reported the US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.29%, its highest level since 2007. It comes after the 30-year yield rose above 5.61%, its highest since 2002, earlier in the session.

squawks.headline: Italy plans to spend €14bn under the EU escape clause to cut energy costs for firms, PM Meloni says
squawks.detail: Italian PM Meloni announced that the spending will be funded through the EU fiscal escape clause. She also said the EU's proposed revision of the ETS carbon trading scheme is inadequate.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham says there are strong indications Iran was involved in the RAF Fairford incident
squawks.detail: The Prime Minister said the UK is working closely with the US administration after five suspects were released on bail, the FT reports. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham says fuel duty is under review ahead of the Budget and rules out unfunded plans
squawks.detail: The Prime Minister said everything is being looked at before the Budget, including fuel duty, and that the Budget cannot contain unfunded plans. He also said the government will do what it can despite difficult public finances.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde calls France's 120%-of-GDP debt serious and says it needs a credible budget path
squawks.detail: In an interview with the newspaper La Croix, ECB President Lagarde said France's debt is serious at 120% of GDP and has no path to coming down, and that the country needs a credible budget trajectory and reforms to restore confidence. She also said the European financial system is more solid now than it was in the 2008 and 2011 crises.

squawks.headline: ECB's Schnabel says strong credit growth suggests financial conditions are not yet restrictive
squawks.detail: In a speech, ECB Executive Board member Schnabel said high costs reach consumers faster when the economy is resilient, and that robust credit dynamics suggest financial conditions are not yet restrictive. She added that the economy might respond more than assumed to the recent rise in global yields, which would dampen price pressures, and that inflation can be brought back to target more gradually if expectations stay anchored.

squawks.headline: US diesel futures rise 4.5% and gasoline futures 2.9% after weekly EIA storage data
squawks.detail: US diesel futures added to earlier gains after the Energy Information Administration's weekly storage report. They were up 4.5%, while gasoline futures held a 2.9% rise.

squawks.headline: US September Chicago PMI jumps to 58.8 from 47.1, well above 51.0 forecast
squawks.detail: The MNI Chicago business barometer for September came in at 58.8, against a consensus of 51.0 and a previous reading of 47.1.

squawks.headline: Analysts estimate Gulf crude exports are back to near pre-war levels
squawks.detail: Goldman Sachs puts crude exports from Persian Gulf producers at 19m b/d and says the recovery came from higher exports through Hormuz. JPMorgan estimates the exports are at 98% of pre-war levels.

squawks.headline: French 10-year yield spread over Germany widens 5bp to 124bp
squawks.detail: The gap between French and German 10-year government bond yields widened by 5bp to 124bp on Wednesday afternoon.

squawks.headline: Fed finalises stress test changes, saying they will not materially change aggregate bank capital requirements
squawks.detail: The Federal Reserve says its changes should cut the year-on-year volatility of bank capital requirements by roughly 50%. Governor Barr voted against the final rule, saying it will weaken the stress test.

squawks.headline: EU says it is open to discussing whatever relationship options the UK proposes
squawks.detail: The EU said it is willing to engage on options the UK may put forward for their relationship. This follows PM Burnham's review of UK relations with the bloc, which he said could include rejoining.

squawks.headline: US August PCE inflation slows to 3.4% y/y against 3.7% forecast; core PCE eases to 3.0% against 3.3% expected
squawks.detail: US data show headline PCE prices at 3.4% y/y, down from 3.7%, and core PCE rising 0.2% m/m against a 0.3% forecast, taking the annual rate to 3.0% from 3.3%. Personal income rose 0.2% m/m against a 0.5% forecast, spending rose 0.9% as expected, and spot gold was reported up 0.6% at $4,206.29/oz after the release.

squawks.headline: US Q2 GDP revised up to 2.2% in final estimate, above 1.5% forecast; Q2 core PCE revised down to 3.3%
squawks.detail: The final US estimate puts second-quarter GDP growth at 2.2%, up from 1.5% and above the 1.5% consensus, while Q2 core PCE prices were revised down to 3.3% from 3.6% and headline Q2 PCE to 5.0% from 5.3%. The US advance goods trade deficit for August widened to $132.6bn against a $115bn forecast.

squawks.headline: US ADP private payrolls rise by 90,000 in September, above forecasts
squawks.detail: The ADP employment change for September came in at 90,000. The posts give different figures for the forecast and the previous reading, but both put the result above consensus.

squawks.headline: German September flash HICP rises to 3.3% y/y from 2.9%, above 3.2% forecast; CPI also 3.3% against 3.1% expected
squawks.detail: Preliminary German figures put September HICP at 3.3% y/y and 0.6% m/m, against forecasts of 3.2% and 0.5% (previous 2.9% and 0.2%). CPI rose to 3.3% y/y from 2.9%, above the 3.1% forecast.

squawks.headline: BoE Governor Bailey urges governments to step up testing of frontier AI models before public release
squawks.detail: In the first of a series of letters on artificial intelligence, the Bank of England governor warned that advanced AI poses sophisticated threats to banking, markets and payments systems, City AM reports.

squawks.headline: Satellite imagery shows China has built a new military support centre in Laos, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that satellite imagery shows China built the facility on farmland in Laos over the past year, extending its overseas military presence into Southeast Asia.

squawks.headline: Japan's economy minister says government and BoJ share the same view on the economy and prices
squawks.detail: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi said there was no difference in understanding between the government and the Bank of Japan on the economy and prices.

squawks.headline: Kremlin confirms contacts with US on possible prisoner exchange and responds to its nuclear warnings to NATO over Kaliningrad
squawks.detail: At the same briefing where it rejected reports of sanctions relief for prisoners, the Kremlin confirmed it is in contact with the United States about a possible prisoner exchange. On Russia's nuclear warnings to NATO over Kaliningrad, it said its diplomats are reminding European leaders of the region's founding documents.

squawks.headline: Kremlin dismisses reports of sanctions relief in return for freeing political prisoners, saying Russia holds none
squawks.detail: The Kremlin calls reports of a possible easing of sanctions in exchange for prisoner releases irrelevant and says Russia has no political prisoners. It also says Putin will address the newly elected parliament later on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: Japan's PM pledges to strengthen supply capacity as prices and rates rise, and to review revenue and spending
squawks.detail: Japan's prime minister says the government will boost supply capacity amid rising prices and interest rates. The PM also says it will assess trends in tax receipts and review revenue and spending.

squawks.headline: Suspected plot against UK airbase used by US forces for Iran strikes was foiled after a suspect called police, Times reports
squawks.detail: The Times reported on Wednesday that one of the men later arrested at the British airbase had alerted police, which led to the suspected plot being thwarted. Reuters carried the report.

squawks.headline: German 10-year Bund auction yields 3.58%, up from 3.39%, with cover falling to 1.2 from 1.5
squawks.detail: Germany's 10-year Bund auction produced an average yield of 3.58%, against 3.39% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.2, down from 1.5.

squawks.headline: BoE FPC says risks are now more likely to crystallise at the same time than in July; gilt repo reforms due early 2027
squawks.detail: The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee said higher oil and gas prices have made the supply shock more protracted and that risky credit, including parts of private credit, remains vulnerable to tighter financing, while markets have so far withstood higher energy prices and bond yields. It said it will set out bank leverage ratio and gilt repo reform proposals in early 2027, that the repo reforms will offset risks from the leverage changes, and that households, companies and banks remain resilient.

squawks.headline: UKMTO receives a late report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency has received a report, made some time after the event, of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. No further details were given.

squawks.headline: Russia extends its diesel export ban for fuel producers to the end of October
squawks.detail: Reports on Wednesday said the Russian government has kept its ban on diesel exports by fuel producers in place until the end of October.

squawks.headline: US formally ends Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports say the United States has officially concluded Operation Inherent Resolve, its military mission in Iraq.

squawks.headline: Witness reports a loud explosion in central Kyiv
squawks.detail: A witness reported hearing a loud explosion in central Kyiv on 30 September. No further details on the cause or damage were given, and no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: PM pledges to amend the state pension triple lock next parliament
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation reported the Prime Minister's commitment to change the triple lock in the next parliament and said the move would help the public finances. No details of the changes were given in the post.

squawks.headline: Burnham says a major review of European policy will consider the UK rejoining the EU
squawks.detail: According to the Financial Times, Andy Burnham said the review will look at the option of rejoining the EU, after saying in his Labour conference speech that Brexit had done more harm than good.

squawks.headline: Trump may unveil plan as soon as Wednesday to use about $54bn of South Korean investment for Alaska LNG project
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that President Trump could set out plans as soon as Wednesday to fund an Alaska liquefied natural gas project from about $54bn of South Korea's pledged strategic investment package. The project faces doubts, according to Reuters.

squawks.headline: Israeli official calls incident on diverted Israel-bound Flydubai flight a terrorist attack, i24 reports
squawks.detail: An Israeli official told broadcaster i24 that the incident on the Flydubai flight bound for Israel, which was diverted to Saudi Arabia, was a terrorist attack. No further details were given.

squawks.headline: OPEC+ expected to hold November output targets steady at Sunday meeting, sources tell Reuters
squawks.detail: Two sources with knowledge of the matter told Reuters that OPEC+ producers are likely to leave production targets for November unchanged when they meet on Sunday.

squawks.headline: Italian September flash CPI rises to 4.2% y/y and HICP to 4.1%, both above 3.7% forecasts
squawks.detail: Italy's preliminary September CPI is up 4.2% y/y (previous 3.3%) and 0.7% m/m (forecast 0.3%). HICP is up 4.1% y/y (previous 3.2%) and 2.0% m/m (forecast 1.7%).

squawks.headline: Australian private credit firm Metrics Credit Partners freezes redemptions from some funds and delays its financial reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Metrics Credit Partners, one of Australia's largest private credit firms, has frozen investor redemptions from some funds and delayed the release of its financial reports. Reuters describes this as the latest sign of stress among non-bank lenders.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham says he is open to rejoining the EU after the next election, with customs union and single market options also possible
squawks.detail: City AM reports that Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday morning that all options for the UK's future relationship with the EU are on the table. He said these include a customs union, the single market or full EU membership.

squawks.headline: BBC reports UK energy bills set to rise 16% in January, below the 24% rise the BoE assumed a couple of weeks ago
squawks.detail: A Resolution Foundation economist cited the BBC report and put the smaller rise down to a slight fall in wholesale gas prices. The Resolution Foundation separately said energy prices will also rise next month.

squawks.headline: Egypt says eight Egyptian crew members from tanker MT Honour 25, hijacked off Somalia, have been released
squawks.detail: Egypt's foreign ministry announced the release of the eight crew members who had been on the hijacked tanker in Somalia.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister tells cabinet Tehran has received a US proposal, government spokesperson says
squawks.detail: A spokesperson for the Iranian government said in a post on X that Foreign Minister Araqchi had told the cabinet about a proposal received from the United States. The post gave no details of what the proposal contains, and the batch reports no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Germany to set up a strategic gas reserve from 2027
squawks.detail: A German Economy Ministry spokesperson said the government will set up a strategic natural gas reserve from 2027. The spokesperson also said the economy minister told state-owned SEFE to raise gas storage because of ongoing geopolitical risks.

squawks.headline: UAE energy minister backs OPEC+ and says demand for additional oil output is rising
squawks.detail: UAE Energy Minister Mazrouei said the country supports the OPEC+ group and will keep coordinating with partners and consumers. He also said demand for extra oil production is increasing.

squawks.headline: Germany orders state-owned energy company SEFE to store gas
squawks.detail: The German government has told SEFE to put gas supply into storage, according to a market newswire report. No volumes or timing were given.

squawks.headline: Flydubai flight bound for Israel is diverted to Saudi Arabia
squawks.detail: A Flydubai flight heading to Israel was diverted to Saudi Arabia, Reuters reported. No reason for the diversion was given.

squawks.headline: North Rhine-Westphalia September CPI rises to 3.3% y/y from 2.9%
squawks.detail: The annual inflation rate in Germany's most populous state rose to 3.3% in September from 2.9% the previous month. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: Italian consumer confidence falls to 91.2, missing 94.4 forecast; manufacturing confidence rises to 91.9
squawks.detail: Italy's consumer confidence index fell to 91.2 in September from 94.5, against a forecast of 94.4. Manufacturing business confidence rose to 91.9 from a revised 90.2, beating the forecast of 90.5.

squawks.headline: Bavaria September CPI rises to 3.2% y/y from 2.9%; up 0.6% m/m
squawks.detail: Bavarian consumer prices rose 3.2% year on year in September, up from 2.9% the previous month, and 0.6% month on month, up from 0.2%. The regional figure comes ahead of Germany's national flash inflation reading.

squawks.headline: Swiss ZEW expectations fall to 2.6 from 12.1
squawks.detail: The Swiss ZEW expectations index fell to 2.6 in the latest reading, down from 12.1 previously.

squawks.headline: Polish airports in Lublin and Rzeszow reopen after closures for military aviation operations
squawks.detail: Poland's Air Traffic Authority said on Wednesday that flights had resumed at Lublin and Rzeszow airports after temporary closures due to military aviation operations, Reuters reported.

squawks.headline: German unemployment rises by 12,000 in September against a forecast rise of 500; jobless rate holds at 6.4%
squawks.detail: German seasonally adjusted unemployment rose by 12,000 in September, against a forecast of 0.5k and a previous rise of 4k, taking the total to 3.012m from 2.996m. The unemployment rate stayed at 6.4%, in line with forecasts; the unadjusted total was 2.994m against 3.061m previously.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation backs proposed changes to the state pension triple lock, citing lower long-run fiscal cost
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says the proposed changes to the triple lock take significant uncertainty and long-run cost out of the public finances while keeping pensioner incomes rising. The post does not give details of the proposals.

squawks.headline: US 30-year Treasury yield rises above 5.61%, its highest level since 2002
squawks.detail: Bloomberg reported that the US 30-year yield went above 5.61% on Tuesday, with inflation concerns and growing bets on Fed rate rises adding to the bond sell-off. The UK 30-year gilt yield stands at 5.307% in the latest snapshot.

squawks.headline: Iran gets US response on seven-day trust-building plan through Qatari mediators in Doha
squawks.detail: Reuters reported that Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi received the US feedback in Doha on Tuesday. An official briefed on the talks said the order of steps was the main sticking point.

squawks.headline: France is the worst-hit G7 government bond market in the sell-off linked to the Iran war
squawks.detail: The FT reported that French bonds have fallen more than any other G7 market as fiscal pressure and political risk build ahead of an election. Vanguard said further losses were possible.

squawks.headline: Riksbank Governor Thedeen says the Swedish economy is stronger than expected
squawks.detail: Sweden's central bank governor, Erik Thedeen, said on Wednesday 30 September that the Swedish economy has been unexpectedly strong. No figures or policy guidance were given in the report.

squawks.headline: US formally ends Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq
squawks.detail: The US has formally brought its Operation Inherent Resolve military mission in Iraq to an end. The input does not report any market reaction.

squawks.headline: Iraq's oil exports average 2.65m bpd in September, including 250,000 bpd via Turkey's Ceyhan port
squawks.detail: A spokesperson for Iraq's oil ministry gave the September average for daily oil exports as 2.65 million barrels per day. Of that, 250,000 bpd went through the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham says rejoining the EU is an option as the government reviews UK relations with the bloc
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the prime minister said full EU membership is an option under consideration. The comments come as the government carries out a review of Britain's relationship with the 27-member bloc.

squawks.headline: Russia extends its ban on diesel exports to the end of October
squawks.detail: Interfax reported on 30 September that Russia has extended its diesel export ban through October. The report gave no market reaction.

squawks.headline: UK energy price cap forecast to rise to nearly £2,000 from January as the Iran war lifts prices
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports a forecast that the household energy price cap will rise to nearly £2,000 for January to March. That would be the biggest increase in four years, driven by higher prices linked to the Iran war.

squawks.headline: French September flash HICP rises to 3.4% y/y against a 3.2% forecast; CPI rises to 3.0% y/y
squawks.detail: France's preliminary September HICP rose to 3.4% y/y, above the 3.2% forecast and up from 2.6%. National CPI rose to 3.0% y/y against a 2.8% forecast, up from 2.4%.

squawks.headline: French flash HICP falls 0.4% m/m against -0.5% forecast; consumer spending drops 0.5% and PPI rises to 4.8% y/y
squawks.detail: Preliminary French HICP fell 0.4% m/m against a forecast of -0.5%, after a 0.7% rise the month before. Consumer spending fell 0.5% m/m against a flat forecast, after a 0.5% rise, and producer prices rose 4.8% y/y, up from 3.4%.

squawks.headline: Drone attacks in Russia's Bryansk region kill one person and injure another, says regional governor
squawks.detail: The governor of Russia's Bryansk region said drone attacks had killed one person and injured another. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Senior source says seven-day plan needs significant changes before progress can be discussed
squawks.detail: Al Arabiya cites a senior source as saying the seven-day proposal needs significant changes before any progress can be discussed. This follows the Iranian foreign minister taking US feedback on the plan back to Tehran after talks in Doha.

squawks.headline: Israeli PM and security minister hold urgent talks with senior security officials, sources say
squawks.detail: Alaraby TV, citing sources, reports that the Israeli Prime Minister and security minister are holding urgent talks with senior security officials. No further details were given.

squawks.headline: UK real household disposable income per head rises 1% in Q2 to £6,577
squawks.detail: ONS figures reported by City AM show real household disposable income per head rose 1% in the second quarter to £6,577. The increase was driven by higher benefit payments, which grew faster than wages.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham plans to change the pensions triple lock from 2030 to fund a national care service and admits a possible funding shortfall
squawks.detail: City AM reports that the Prime Minister announced the triple lock will be adjusted from 2030, in effect becoming a double lock, with the savings going to a new national care service. He acknowledged the plans may face a shortfall, and economists cited in the report said taxes would need to rise.

squawks.headline: Ministers tell business groups the uncapped overnight stay levy will let mayors take on more borrowing
squawks.detail: City AM reports that at Labour's Business Day, ministers told leading business groups that the new uncapped tourist tax would allow mayors to increase their borrowing.

squawks.headline: Oil rises after Trump denies he is willing to ease sanctions on Iran
squawks.detail: Reuters reports oil prices rose on Wednesday after US President Trump denied he would ease sanctions on Iran, while Qatar pushed for peace talks. Prices had fallen in the previous session as Middle East crude supply recovered.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham says cutting the welfare bill will allow the UK to meet its defence goals
squawks.detail: The Prime Minister linked lower welfare spending to paying for the UK's defence spending commitments. No figures were given.

squawks.headline: UK Q2 business investment rises 5.2% y/y against a 0.8% forecast; exports up 2.8% q/q, government spending down 0.5%
squawks.detail: The Q2 GDP breakdown shows business investment up 1.8% q/q, gross fixed capital formation up 0.9% q/q against a 1.2% forecast, and private consumption up 0.3% q/q, in line with forecasts. Exports grew 2.8% q/q and imports were flat; both had been forecast at 0.5%. Government spending fell 0.5% q/q against a forecast of -0.3%.

squawks.headline: German real retail sales rise 1.3% m/m, below the 1.5% forecast, after a 3.4% fall
squawks.detail: German real retail sales rose 1.3% month on month, against a forecast of 1.5%. The previous reading was a 3.4% fall.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham says the UK should consider options for its EU relationship, including eventually rejoining
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday that Britain should weigh options for its future relationship with the European Union, including rejoining the bloc in the longer run. He is stepping up efforts to rebuild ties with Europe.

squawks.headline: German import prices rise 8.3% y/y and 1% m/m, both above forecasts
squawks.detail: German import prices rose 8.3% year on year, against a forecast of 8% and 6.8% previously. On the month they rose 1%, against a forecast of 0.7% and 0.2% previously.

squawks.headline: UK GDP grows 0.5% q/q and 1.4% y/y, above forecasts of 0.4% and 1.2%
squawks.detail: UK GDP grew 0.5% quarter on quarter against a forecast of 0.4% and a previous reading of 0.4%, and 1.4% year on year against a forecast and previous reading of 1.2%. Business investment rose 1.75% q/q, against a forecast of 1.7% and a previous reading of 1.7%.

squawks.headline: UK current account deficit narrows to 19.932bn, smaller than the 25.5bn forecast
squawks.detail: The UK current account showed a deficit of 19.932bn, against a forecast of 25.5bn and 22.134bn previously.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister takes US feedback on seven-day proposal to Tehran after Doha talks with Qatari mediators
squawks.detail: Foreign Minister Araghchi met Qatari mediators in Doha on Tuesday night and received the US response to the seven-day proposal, which he is due to discuss in Tehran on Wednesday, according to an official briefed on the talks. The official said the main disagreement between the US and Iran concerns sequencing rather than the plan's elements.

squawks.headline: Kazakhstan restarts enforcement proceedings to recover a 2.3tn tenge fine from the NCOC oil consortium
squawks.detail: Kazakhstan has restarted enforcement proceedings to recover a 2.3 trillion tenge fine from North Caspian Operating Company (NCOC), according to an Interfax report.

squawks.headline: Gold edges lower as bets on a Fed rate hike and Middle East tensions support the US dollar
squawks.detail: Gold prices slipped in early trading on 30 September, with the move attributed to bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike and Middle East tensions supporting the US dollar. No figures were given in the report.

squawks.headline: Russia says it struck a Kyiv communications centre and energy facilities in the Kyiv region overnight
squawks.detail: Interfax, citing Russia's Defence Ministry, reported an overnight strike on a communications centre in Kyiv. The ministry also said energy system facilities in the Kyiv region were hit in what it called a massive strike.

squawks.headline: Vanguard says France's credit is degrading as French borrowing costs rise sharply
squawks.detail: The FT reports the warning from Vanguard. It says the Iran war has added to fiscal pressures on Paris ahead of a budget battle.

squawks.headline: Experts put the cost of a fully funded social care model for England at £18.7bn
squawks.detail: The FT reports experts saying the prime minister's planned national care service would still leave some elderly people selling their homes to pay for care. They said a model covering all costs would cost £18.7bn and would probably need tax rises.

squawks.headline: Dollar is on course for its largest monthly gain against the euro in 14 months
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the dollar is near this year's high against the euro. It cites US growth and rising US interest rates, set against energy and debt concerns in Europe.

squawks.headline: Oil prices stay elevated even as Persian Gulf exports recover
squawks.detail: The WSJ reports that oil prices remain high despite a recovery in exports from the Persian Gulf. The report gave no price figures.

squawks.headline: China imposes an extra 55% tariff on Brazilian beef imports from 1 October
squawks.detail: China's commerce ministry said the additional 55% tariff will be charged on top of the rate that currently applies.

squawks.headline: Poland temporarily shuts Rzeszow and Lublin airports as military aircraft operate; air defences put on readiness
squawks.detail: Polish authorities said the two airports were closed temporarily because of military aviation activity. The Polish army said its ground-based air defence and radar reconnaissance systems had reached readiness and that its operational command was monitoring the situation.

squawks.headline: White House holds talks on a possible diesel export ban ahead of the US midterms
squawks.detail: The FT reports that the White House is weighing a ban on diesel exports. The report describes a lobbying fight involving President Trump, with oil majors on one side and senior Republicans on the other, who warn of voter anger over high fuel prices.

squawks.headline: Japan's 2-year JGB auction draws a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.89
squawks.detail: Japan's Ministry of Finance held a 2-year government bond auction on Wednesday, which drew a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.89.

squawks.headline: China's finance ministry to reopen 80bn yuan of 10-year bonds on 9 October
squawks.detail: China's finance ministry said it will sell 80bn yuan of reopened 10-year bonds on 9 October and 20bn yuan of 28-day bills on 8 October.

squawks.headline: US forces due to leave their remaining bases in Iraq; Iran's IRGC urges US voters to oust Trump's allies
squawks.detail: Reuters reported US troops were due to withdraw from their last bases in Iraq on Wednesday, a departure welcomed by Tehran. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps called on Americans to vote Trump's congressional allies out of office.

squawks.headline: Global bonds head for their worst month in years in September
squawks.detail: Reuters reported global bonds weakening on Wednesday, pressured by worsening government finances, heavy issuance and rising inflation. It said energy costs remain high as the US-Israeli war on Iran enters its seventh month.

squawks.headline: South Korean spy agency estimates about 9,000 North Korean soldiers are in Russia
squawks.detail: A South Korean lawmaker, citing the spy agency, said there was no sign of further North Korean troop deployments to Russia and that the two countries had cooperated on ballistic missile shipments. The lawmaker also put the chance of North Korea-US talks at the APEC summit at 50%.

squawks.headline: China's military runs readiness patrols around Scarborough Shoal
squawks.detail: Chinese forces carried out readiness patrols in the sea and airspace around Scarborough Shoal on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: China's RatingDog September PMIs beat forecasts: manufacturing 52.1, services 51.6, composite 52.4
squawks.detail: The private RatingDog survey put manufacturing at 52.1 against a 51.7 forecast and 51.5 in August, and services at 51.6 against 51.3 expected and 51.4 previously. The composite rose to 52.4 from 52.1, and Reuters reported services growth at a three-month high on stronger new orders.

squawks.headline: Brent rises more than $1 to $103.73 after Trump denies Iran sanctions relief
squawks.detail: Brent crude futures gained more than $1 to $103.73 a barrel in Asian trading after President Trump denied that sanctions relief for Iran was planned.

squawks.headline: South Korea's military demands North Korea halt border fortification work and says troops were badly hurt by mines
squawks.detail: South Korea's military said North Korea's fortification activity is raising tensions on the peninsula and demanded that it stop immediately and apologise. It also said some of its personnel were seriously injured by North Korean mines.

squawks.headline: China's official September PMIs: manufacturing 50.1, non-manufacturing 50.2, composite 50.7
squawks.detail: NBS manufacturing PMI rose to 50.1 from 49.8, in line with forecasts. Non-manufacturing rose to 50.2 from 49.0, above the 49.2 forecast, and the composite rose to 50.7 from 49.5.

squawks.headline: Australian August CPI rises to 4.0% y/y from 3.5%, just below the 4.1% forecast; trimmed mean steady at 3.6%
squawks.detail: Headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m against a 0.5% estimate, while trimmed mean inflation was 3.6% y/y (0.2% m/m) and the weighted median was 3.6% y/y. Building approvals fell 6.1% m/m against a forecast 1.0% fall, and private sector credit rose 0.6% m/m.

squawks.headline: Lloyds survey: UK business confidence falls to its lowest in 17 months in September
squawks.detail: Lloyds' monthly survey shows British firms at their least confident since April 2025. Executives also took a darker view of the global outlook, with the Iran war reported to be raising costs.

squawks.headline: PBOC injects 833.5bn yuan through overnight reverse repos and conducts no 7-day operations
squawks.detail: China's central bank added 833.5bn yuan of liquidity through overnight reverse repos and held no 7-day reverse repo operations, according to its statement.

squawks.headline: PBOC sets yuan midpoint at its strongest level since 2 February 2023
squawks.detail: China's central bank set the yuan's daily reference rate at its strongest level since 2 February 2023.

squawks.headline: China announces mortgage subsidies for first-time buyers and cuts a policy interest rate
squawks.detail: Beijing is offering support to first-time homebuyers and has cut a policy rate as part of efforts to lift growth, the FT reports. Mainland property stock indices were indicated lower after the announcement, with the Hang Seng Mainland Properties Index seen down 1.3% and the CSI 300 Real Estate Index seen down 5%.

squawks.headline: PBOC sets yuan midpoint at 6.7351 per dollar, weaker than the 6.7025 estimate
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China sets the daily yuan reference rate at 6.7351 to the dollar. Market estimates had been 6.7025.

squawks.headline: 10-year JGB yield rises 1.0bp to 3.095%
squawks.detail: The 10-year Japanese government bond yield is up 1.0bp at 3.095% in Asian trading. WSJ reports short-dated JGBs gaining alongside shorter US Treasurys.

squawks.headline: Russian missile strike on Kyiv hits homes and energy sites, cutting power to parts of the capital
squawks.detail: Witnesses reported explosions in Kyiv from about 00:25 UTC. Later reports described a heavy ballistic missile attack that hit residential areas and energy infrastructure, with outages in parts of the city.

squawks.headline: US states act to curb diesel and petrol prices after months of supply disruption
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that US states are taking steps to hold down fuel prices, which have risen sharply in recent months. It links the rise to disruption from the US war on Iran, Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries and low global inventories.

squawks.headline: South Korea may use surplus tax revenue to cut bond issuance and buy back bonds if yields rise too far
squawks.detail: South Korea's finance minister says the ministry is watching the bond market closely and may use excess tax revenue to reduce issuance. He adds that treasury bond buybacks and other steps are possible if yields rise too sharply.

squawks.headline: US forces leave their remaining bases in Iraq
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that US troops leave their last bases in Iraq on Wednesday. It says the move raises fears of a security vacuum that could help Iranian-backed militias and Islamic State.

squawks.headline: Israel's finance minister calls for Gaza-style operations in the West Bank and a large arms build-up
squawks.detail: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich calls for the approach used in Gaza to be applied in the West Bank, including flattening a neighbourhood in Qalqilya where a tunnel was found. He also calls for an arms build-up larger than the army is seeking and for Israel to expand defence exports.

squawks.headline: ANZ survey: New Zealand business confidence falls to 51.9 in September from 53.7
squawks.detail: ANZ's September survey shows business confidence at 51.9, down from 53.7. Its own-activity outlook slips to 47.9 from 48.2.

squawks.headline: Japan's August industrial output falls 1.7% m/m against forecasts of a rise; retail sales growth slows to 2.7% y/y
squawks.detail: Government data show industrial output fell 1.7% on the month, after -0.2% previously, against forecasts of a 1.3% to 1.7% rise; retail sales rose 2.7% year on year against forecasts of 3.2% to 3.3%. Manufacturers expect output to rise 3.2% in September and 3.1% in October.

squawks.headline: US trade representative says tariff caps in trade deals will be considered in setting Section 301 excess capacity tariffs
squawks.detail: USTR Greer said caps agreed in trade deals will be taken into account when setting tariffs under the Section 301 probe into excess capacity.

squawks.headline: Japan, US and Europe to agree a steel monitoring framework, Yomiuri reports
squawks.detail: Japan's Yomiuri newspaper reports that Japan, the US and Europe are set to agree a framework for monitoring steel.

squawks.headline: China threatens a firm response if the EU keeps imposing limits on Chinese firms and products
squawks.detail: China's commerce ministry called tougher trade measures under consideration by EU states protectionist and unilateral. EU trade chief Sefcovic said he is pushing for G20 and WTO reforms on excess industrial capacity and working with the US and other allies to secure critical mineral supply chains.

squawks.headline: UK car output rises 5.7% y/y in August to 40,872 units, SMMT says
squawks.detail: The Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders reports UK vehicle production of 40,872 units in August, up 5.7% on a year earlier.

squawks.headline: South Korea's August industrial output falls 2.2% y/y against a forecast 4% rise; retail sales fall 1.8% m/m
squawks.detail: The statistics office reports industrial output down 4.8% on the month and 2.2% on the year, against a poll forecast of a 4% annual rise. Service sector output rose 0.5% on the month and retail sales fell 1.8%.

squawks.headline: Senior Saudi official denies any meeting between Saudi and Israeli officials
squawks.detail: A senior Saudi official denied that any Saudi official had met Israeli officials, according to posts late on 29 September.

squawks.headline: Burnham says Labour will pledge to drop the pensions triple lock in a future manifesto; Reform UK and Conservatives attack the plan
squawks.detail: On Tuesday the Prime Minister said he would lead Labour on a manifesto pledge to scrap the triple lock, a policy previously backed by all major parties. Reform UK and Conservative leaders criticised the move, City AM reports.

squawks.headline: UK chief executives back pensions triple lock action but prepare for possible tax rises in next month's Budget, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that business leaders welcomed the government's action on the pensions triple lock. They are preparing for possible tax rises in the Budget due next month and say the focus from Burnham and Healey on the cost of business has left them unclear.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says there is time to assess data before the next hike and expects one more rise before year-end
squawks.detail: New York Fed President John Williams said on Tuesday that the Federal Reserve has time to weigh incoming economic data before deciding when to raise rates again. He added that one more increase is likely before the end of the year, Reuters reported.

squawks.headline: US offers to lend up to 40m barrels of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, its last batch under a global release deal
squawks.detail: The US government said on Tuesday it is offering energy companies loans of up to 40 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. This is the final US tranche of a global agreement to release reserves after the war on Iran.

squawks.headline: North Korea rejects Seoul's findings on DMZ mine blast that injured South Korean troops and warns of a catastrophic situation
squawks.detail: North Korean state news agency KCNA said South Korea had fabricated its findings on the blast, denied that North Korean troops crossed the military border and warned that the South could face a catastrophic situation. It also said the barriers it is building along the border are an exercise of sovereignty with no military purpose.

squawks.headline: API data show crude stocks at the Cushing hub up 0.233m barrels
squawks.detail: American Petroleum Institute weekly data show Cushing crude inventories rose by 0.233m barrels, following a 2.082m-barrel rise in the previous week; no forecast was given.

squawks.headline: Trump is set to announce a $54bn Alaska LNG plan, with funding reported to come from a South Korea investment deal
squawks.detail: President Trump is due to set out a $54bn liquefied natural gas project in Alaska. People familiar with the plan say the money will come from an investment agreement with South Korea.

squawks.headline: US 30-year Treasury yield hits its highest level since 2002 as inflation and borrowing concerns weigh
squawks.detail: Treasury yields rose on concerns over persistent inflation, government spending and rising corporate borrowing, with the 30-year yield at its highest since 2002. The S&P 500 closed down 0.2%, the Dow down 0.3% and the Nasdaq 100 up 0.2%.

squawks.headline: API data show US crude stocks up 1.019m barrels, against a forecast draw of 1.9m
squawks.detail: The American Petroleum Institute reported a weekly US crude inventory build of 1.019m barrels, against a forecast 1.9m draw and a previous build of 1.786m. The gasoline and distillate figures were reported earlier.

squawks.headline: API data show US gasoline stocks up 2.991m barrels and distillate stocks down 0.286m barrels
squawks.detail: Weekly American Petroleum Institute figures show gasoline inventories rose by 2.991m barrels, after a 2.16m draw the previous week. Distillate stocks fell by 0.286m barrels, compared with a 2.164m draw previously.

squawks.headline: UAE vice president visits Saudi Arabia, the first senior UAE visit since the rift between the two Gulf states last year
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and the Saudi defence minister on Tuesday. It is the first visit to the kingdom by a senior UAE official since a deep rift opened between the two countries last year.

squawks.headline: European gas storage is reported well below usual levels before winter after curbs on Hormuz tanker traffic
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that restrictions on tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz disrupted Europe's usual summer refilling of gas stocks, leaving reserves far lower than normal as the EU looks for extra supply before winter. The report gives no storage figures.

squawks.headline: Grynspan reportedly leads fourth UN Security Council straw poll for next UN Secretary-General
squawks.detail: Reports say Rebeca Grynspan won the most votes in the fourth straw poll to choose the next UN Secretary-General. The reports gave no vote counts.

squawks.headline: US bank regulators find no deficiencies in resolution plans of 15 banks with more than $250bn in assets
squawks.detail: US bank regulators reported on 29 September that their review found no deficiencies in the 'living wills' filed by 15 banks, each with assets above $250bn.

squawks.headline: US stocks and bonds fall as inflation concerns keep yields elevated
squawks.detail: A US market wrap reported that equities and Treasuries both fell on Tuesday, with inflation concerns keeping yields high.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says rising bond yields tighten financial conditions at the margin
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said higher yields tighten financial conditions at the margin, but he does not see them as a sign of changing longer-run inflation expectations. He also said AI has not so far caused big changes in job levels.

squawks.headline: Russian glide bomb attack on Ukraine's Sumy kills two, officials say
squawks.detail: Officials said Russian glide bombs hit homes and a school in the northern Ukrainian city of Sumy on Tuesday, killing two people and injuring six, Reuters reported.

squawks.headline: Kpler: Middle East oil shipments rise to nearly 80% of prewar levels despite US-Iran tensions
squawks.detail: Research firm Kpler found that oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and on routes bypassing it reached nearly 80% of prewar levels last week, Semafor reported.

squawks.headline: UN raises alarm over reports that a Myanmar military air strike near the Bangladesh border killed 50 people
squawks.detail: On Tuesday the United Nations expressed alarm at reports that a Myanmar military air strike near the border with Bangladesh killed 50 people and wounded dozens more, according to Reuters. Many of the wounded are reported to be in a critical condition.

squawks.headline: Fed Governor Barr argues further US rate hikes are likely needed to bring inflation down
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said on Tuesday that high energy prices and a jump in AI-related investment have set back progress towards the Fed's 2% inflation target, Reuters reported. He argued again for more rate increases.

squawks.headline: Iran's presidency says Tehran will make no concessions on its nuclear rights
squawks.detail: Iran's President's Office said the country would not compromise on its nuclear rights and called this a central point of the President's speech, according to state broadcaster IRIB News.

squawks.headline: OPEC+ delegates signal the group is likely to keep its planned steady output quotas
squawks.detail: Delegates say OPEC+ is expected to stay with its existing plan of steady production quotas. No figures were given.

squawks.headline: Somali pirates kill five crew of hijacked tanker MT Honour 25 before security forces rescue it, Puntland says
squawks.detail: Authorities in Puntland say pirates killed five crew members on board the hijacked tanker MT Honour 25. Security forces then rescued the vessel.

squawks.headline: Iran warns regional states of consequences over Netanyahu's visit to the UAE
squawks.detail: Fars News reported that Iran's Foreign Ministry warned countries in the region of the consequences of Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's visit to the United Arab Emirates.

squawks.headline: BoE's Taylor doubts a single rate hike is practical without fuelling market bets on further increases
squawks.detail: Reuters reported on Tuesday that Bank of England MPC member Alan Taylor said it was unclear whether the Bank could make a single rate hike to curb inflation without prompting unwarranted market speculation of further hikes. At the time of the snapshot the 2-year gilt yield was 3.92% and 1-year SONIA OIS was 3.661%.

squawks.headline: US consumer confidence falls to near 12-1/2-year low in September
squawks.detail: Reuters reported that US consumer confidence dropped sharply in September to its lowest in nearly 12-1/2 years. Households expect business and labour market conditions to worsen over the next six months, against a backdrop of the Middle East conflict and rising interest rates.

squawks.headline: Euro falls to 16-month low against the dollar at $1.13415
squawks.detail: The euro was last down 0.26% at $1.13415, its lowest level against the US dollar in 16 months.

squawks.headline: Oil futures settle lower: Brent down 2.56% at $102.59/bbl, US crude down 3.48% at $89.38/bbl
squawks.detail: Brent crude futures settled $2.69 lower at $102.59 a barrel. US crude futures settled $3.22 lower at $89.38 a barrel.

squawks.headline: US sanctions 10 individuals and entities accused of procuring weapons for Iran's defence ministry
squawks.detail: The US Treasury Department said on Tuesday that the 10 individuals and entities it has sanctioned include some based in China, Hong Kong and Pakistan. It said they helped Iran's Ministry of Defence obtain weapons and components.

squawks.headline: Traders scale back bets on an October Fed hike and now price one more hike by year-end after Williams remarks
squawks.detail: Market pricing moved after New York Fed President Williams said there was no urgency for further action following September's hike. Traders now expect only one more Fed rate hike by the end of the year.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says AI is pushing up asset valuations and early data show it lifting productivity
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said AI is raising asset market valuations, which strengthens the wealth effect. He added that some data are beginning to show AI supporting productivity gains.

squawks.headline: BP offers six-year labour contract at its 440,000 bpd Whiting refinery as union talks go on
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that BP on Tuesday proposed a six-year labour contract for workers at its 440,000-barrel-per-day Whiting refinery in Indiana. Negotiations with United Steelworkers Local 7-1 are continuing.

squawks.headline: Mediators step up efforts to end the stalemate between the US and Iran, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that mediators are working to break the deadlock between Washington and Tehran. The report gave no further details.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams expects inflation to ease as the largest shocks have mostly passed, and says US is less exposed to energy
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said inflation should come down because the biggest shocks have largely run their course. He added that energy prices still matter a great deal to the economy, but the US is less exposed to them than in the past.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says monetary policy is still somewhat accommodative despite the latest rate hike
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem described the US policy stance as still somewhat accommodative after the Federal Reserve's most recent rate increase. These remarks add to his earlier comments today.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem suggests anonymously linking rate dots to economic projections to improve the SEP
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said the Fed's Summary of Economic Projections could be improved by connecting each participant's anonymous rate projection to their economic forecasts. The remark was reported on 29 September.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says about half of current inflation comes from persistent demand pressure, with long-run expectations anchored at 2%
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said roughly half of inflation now reflects persistent demand pressure. He added that inflation expectations remain consistent with 2% inflation over the long run.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says the case for looking through supply shocks weakens when shocks come one after another
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said repeated supply shocks raise the risk that broader inflation becomes entrenched. In the same remarks he described US growth as strong and the labour market as being in a good place, adding that this depends on growth continuing.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says rates cannot be eased on expected AI productivity gains, with AI capex currently adding to demand pressure
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said the AI capital spending boom is driving demand, and productivity gains and supply relief are not yet visible.

squawks.headline: Germany cuts fuel tax from 1 October as Middle East crisis pushes up fuel prices
squawks.detail: A CGTN report says the German government is reducing fuel tax from 1 October to ease pressure from rising fuel prices linked to the Middle East crisis.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams sees one further hike as likely this year if the economy performs as expected, but no urgency after September's hike
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said policy will respond to data, he projects US inflation at 3.5% this year and back at the 2% target in 2028, and it is imperative that high inflation does not become entrenched. He sees US GDP growth of 2.25% this year and unemployment at 4% over 2027, and said AI investment is an increasingly big issue for inflation.

squawks.headline: IFS publishes analysis of PM Burnham's triple lock changes, which take effect in 2030–31
squawks.detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies has published an assessment of the changes to the state pension triple lock announced by Prime Minister Andy Burnham. It says the reform comes into effect in 2030–31.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada's Gravelle says government bond purchases for the balance sheet may not start until 2028
squawks.detail: Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Gravelle said purchases of Government of Canada bonds are likely to start later than planned and may not begin until 2028.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures drop more than 2% as Middle East oil flows show signs of recovery
squawks.detail: Brent crude futures fell by more than 2% late on 29 September, with the move put down to signs that crude flows from the Middle East are recovering.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says oil prices could fall fairly quickly but getting refineries back online is the harder problem
squawks.detail: In further remarks on 29 September, Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said oil prices could come down relatively quickly, but the bigger challenge is restoring refinery operations. He also told listeners to watch productivity.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee calls for a rethink of looking through supply shocks after five and a half years of inflation above target
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said the approach of looking through supply shocks needs revisiting. He described inflation's five and a half years above the Fed's target as playing with fire.

squawks.headline: Puntland forces free a petroleum products tanker that Somali pirates seized in April
squawks.detail: Security forces in Somalia's semi-autonomous Puntland state rescued the Palau-flagged tanker MT Honour 25, according to Puntland state television on Tuesday, as reported by Reuters.

squawks.headline: UK counter-terrorism police find no explosive devices in probe into suspected plot against airbase used by US forces
squawks.detail: Counter-terrorism police said on Tuesday that no improvised explosive devices had been found in their investigation of a suspected plot targeting a British airbase used by US forces for strikes on Iran, Reuters reported.

squawks.headline: Fed's Goolsbee says the Federal Reserve Act does not require the Fed to keep bond or stock markets happy
squawks.detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said the Fed's mandate contains no requirement to satisfy the bond market or to avoid surprising equity markets.

squawks.headline: BP's Whiting refinery proposes a six-year contract to union as labour talks continue
squawks.detail: BP's Whiting refinery said it has offered the USW 7-1 union a six-year contract term with a longer notice period before any strike or lockout. It said talks with union representatives will continue.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barr says the US economy is strong, inflation has been too high and AI is pushing up costs in the short term
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Barr made the remarks in an interview with Detroit radio station WJR. He said inflation running too high has left people frustrated and uncertain.

squawks.headline: UN Security Council extends mandate of international security force in Haiti by six months
squawks.detail: The UN Security Council voted on Tuesday to extend the mandate of the international force fighting armed groups in Haiti by six months, Reuters reports. The vote follows fresh killings by gangs.

squawks.headline: White House reportedly weighs European diesel reserve release as a way to avoid a US diesel export ban
squawks.detail: Politico reports that the White House is looking at a release of Europe's diesel reserves as an alternative to a US export ban. This follows earlier reports that Washington is pressing the EU to release emergency diesel stocks.
